the Rabbis who dispute RYBN on the skins of sheratzim
the first baraita (107a.7-107b.1): divrei RYBN; vachachamim omrim
the Sages of the first baraita
the second baraita (107b.2): bisheratzim sheyesh lahem orot

props.gloss_en: the mishna: the eight creeping animals -- one who wounds them is liable
from the mishna's 'one who wounds them is liable' it follows that they have skin
Shmuel: the tanna [of the wounding clause] is R' Yochanan ben Nuri
RYBN: the eight sheratzim have skins
Rav: [the mishna can be] even [according to] the Rabbis
the Rabbis dispute RYBN only regarding impurity
as it is written 'these are the impure for you' -- to include that their skins are like their flesh
but regarding Shabbat even the Rabbis concede [that they have skins]
the baraita: one who traps one of the eight sheratzim, one who wounds them, is liable -- the words of RYBN
and the Sages say: there is no skin except for what the Sages enumerated
[read literally:] only those the Sages enumerated have [distinct] skin
on the contrary: those the Sages enumerated have no [distinct] skin
Abaye: this is what it says -- skin is distinct from flesh only for those the Sages did not enumerate
Rava: rather, this is what it says -- skin imparts impurity like flesh only for those the Sages enumerated
it is taught: RYBN -- the eight sheratzim have skins, and [the skins] do not impart impurity
Rav Adda bar Mattana: resolve it thus -- and the Sages say: regarding impurity, there is no skin for those the Sages enumerated
the second baraita: one who traps one of the eight sheratzim, one who wounds them, is liable -- for sheratzim that have skins
and what is a wound that does not return? the blood is gathered, though it did not come out
Rav Ashi: the tanna kamma [of the second baraita] is R' Yehuda, who goes by the texture [of the skin]
R' Yehuda goes by the texture [of the skin]
R' Yehuda: the letaah is like the chulda
teach [in the first baraita]: 'the words of RYBN and his disputants'
[that] a wound [is one that] does not return [is known] from 'can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard his chavarburot'
if you say [chavarburotav means] that it stands in spots upon spots
rather [chavarburotav are wounds], like the Cushite
as the Cushite's skin does not return, so a wound does not return
